sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Lenoir County, NC?
sections.html:
Deeds for Lenoir County land are recorded at the Register of Deeds office at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston, NC 28501. The mailing address is PO Box 3289, Kinston, NC 28502, and the office takes calls at 252-559-6420.

The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30am to 5:00pm, and the same hours apply to recording. Beyond deeds, mortgages and deeds of trust, the same counter handles maps, assumed names, notary oaths, military discharges and vital records, so a seller who also needs a certified copy of a family record can ask for it on the same visit.

North Carolina counties elect their register of deeds, and under G.S. 161-1 the term is two years. The Lenoir County office reads and applies the state recording statutes, so a seller gets the same rules here that apply in every other North Carolina county, only with a Kinston counter and a Kinston fee sheet.

sections.h2: How does a Lenoir County deed get recorded step by step?
sections.html:
A deed is signed and acknowledged first, then delivered to the Kinston office, either on paper or electronically, with the excise tax and the page fee. The register of deeds stamps it, indexes it by grantor and grantee, and assigns book and page references.

  • Have the deed prepared and notarized, usually by the closing attorney handling the sale.
  • Pay the recording fee and the excise tax before the register accepts the instrument.
  • Present the deed in person, by mail to PO Box 3289, or through e-recording.
  • Keep the recording receipt and the book and page numbers for your files.

Lenoir County announces that its office accepts e-recording and points users to Simplifile at (801) 223-1046 for enrollment. Debit and credit cards work at the counter with a small usage fee. When you order a birth or marriage certificate by mail, the office asks for payment in full by cash or money order, not personal checks, plus a self-addressed stamped envelope and a copy of photo ID.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record documents in Lenoir County?
sections.html:
Recording charges are set by state law, and the Lenoir County office collects them before it files an instrument. The county links its own fee schedule from the Register of Deeds page, so ask the office to confirm the current sheet when you are ready to record.

North Carolina recording fees collected by the register of deeds (G.S. 161-10)
ItemFee as the statute prints it
Instruments in general$26.00 for the first 15 pages, $4.00 for each additional page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64.00 for the first 35 pages, $4.00 for each additional page
Satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage or deed of trustNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 for the first page, $2.00 for each additional page
Nonstandard document$25.00 added

The statute calls these fees complete and exclusive. The payoff of a mortgage is recorded as a cancellation at no charge, which helps when you are clearing an old lien before a sale.

sections.h2: How is the deed excise tax charged in Lenoir County?
sections.html:
The state excise tax on a deed is one dollar for each $500 of the consideration or value conveyed, with any fraction of $500 counted as a full unit. G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor, meaning the seller, responsible for paying it to the register of deeds of the county where the land lies before the instrument is recorded.

The register splits the money. Half stays with the county general fund and the other half goes to the Department of Revenue each month, less refunds and the county's allowance. In practice the closing attorney collects the tax from the seller's proceeds and hands it to the Kinston office with the deed, so a seller rarely writes a separate check.

sections.h2: Why does recording matter to someone selling a Lenoir County house?
sections.html:
Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance or contract to convey land does not protect the buyer against lien creditors or later purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land is. Priority follows the order of registration, by time.

That rule is why buyers and lenders insist on same-day recording, and why a seller should treat recording as part of the sale, not a formality afterward. If an unrecorded deed sits in a drawer while a judgment or second sale is recorded first, the earlier paper can lose.

The same statute reaches options and leases longer than three years, a right of first refusal and a right of first offer. If your Lenoir County property carries any of those, ask the closing attorney to search the Kinston index for them before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What is Lenoir County like for sellers?
sections.html:
Lenoir County is an eastern North Carolina county with Kinston as its seat and La Grange and Pink Hill among its other communities. The Census Bureau counts 55,837 residents for July 1, 2025, down from 59,495 in 2010 and about level with the 55,122 counted in 2020.

  • Housing units: 27,402 (July 2025 estimate).
  • Owner-occupied rate: 59.2%, which leaves a large renter share.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $120,500 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Median gross rent: $861.
  • Median household income: $45,143 in 2024 dollars.
  • Land area: 399.09 square miles.

The county was chartered in 1791 from land that had belonged to Bath, Craven, Johnston and Dobbs counties. Kinston was established in 1762 as Kingston, and the courthouse stands at the same corner of Queen and King Streets where the first frame courthouse went up in 1779.

With homes valued near $120,500 at the median, a recording fee schedule can feel large next to the sale price, so check the fee sheet early and plan for it at closing.

sections.h2: How does Lenoir County property tax tie into a sale?
sections.html:
The Lenoir County Tax Department at 101 North Queen Street, reachable at 252-527-7174, lists, appraises and bills property, and it keeps the transfer records that follow each recorded deed. Real estate is on a permanent listing system, so an owner does not file a yearly listing unless the value changes, while taxable personal property such as mobile homes, boats and unlicensed vehicles must be listed in January or face a 10 percent late penalty.

The county said its last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2017 and described a new one effective January 1, 2025. The 2026 real estate appeal window closed April 23, 2026 when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourned, and the county stated that the 2027 window opens January 1, 2027.

State law makes taxes due September 1 and adds interest from January 6, first 2 percent and then three-fourths of one percent a month. Under G.S. 105-355 the lien attaches on the listing date, so an unpaid bill follows the parcel into a sale. Ask the tax office for the current balance, then have the closing attorney pay it from the seller's proceeds.

sections.h2: What should I check before I record or sell in Lenoir County?
sections.html:
Start with the record itself. Search the Kinston index under your name and the prior owner's name, and ask the office what it shows for open deeds of trust, easements and recorded plats.

  • Confirm every owner on the last recorded deed, including heirs if the owner has died.
  • Ask the tax office for any unpaid bill and any present-use value deferral.
  • Make sure old mortgages have a recorded cancellation.
  • Decide whether you will record on paper or enroll in e-recording.
  • Budget for the excise tax and recording fees before you agree on a net price.

If the house is inherited, call the clerk of superior court for the Lenoir County estate steps before anyone signs a deed, and keep a certified death certificate on hand. The Register of Deeds office keeps death records.

faqs.q: Where is the Lenoir County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is at 101 North Queen Street, Kinston, NC 28501, with a mailing address of PO Box 3289, Kinston, NC 28502. It is open Monday through Friday from 8:30am to 5:00pm, and the phone is 252-559-6420.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Lenoir County?
faqs.a: Yes, the Lenoir County Register of Deeds lists e-recording on its page and sends interested users to Simplifile at (801) 223-1046 to enroll. Many closing attorneys already use it for sales.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax in Lenoir County?
faqs.a: The seller pays it, as the transferor under G.S. 105-228.30, before the deed is recorded. The rate is $1.00 for each $500.00 of value or fractional part of it, and the closing attorney normally takes it from the seller's proceeds.

faqs.q: Does it cost anything to record the payoff of a mortgage in Lenoir County?
faqs.a: No, North Carolina charges nothing to record a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage under G.S. 161-10. Ask your lender to send the cancellation to Kinston after payoff.

faqs.q: How do I pay property tax owed on a Lenoir County house I am selling?
faqs.a: Contact the Lenoir County Tax Department at 252-527-7174 for the balance, and have the closing attorney pay it at settlement. Taxes are due September 1 and interest starts January 6, so older balances grow.
